instances: Benzecri.exemple_carre_somme: [0,1]² = [0,1]×{0} + {0}×[0,1] in ℝ×ℝ (Déf. 1, a Lean term)

Benzecri.disque_non_somme_segments: for all a b c d, the closed unit disc {p | p.1²+p.2² ≤ 1} of ℝ² is NOT IsSommeConvexes of ![segment a b, segment c d]; stronger: Benzecri.disque_ne_somme_segments (not even the Minkowski sum; degenerate segments included)

Benzecri.exemple_carre_classes and Benzecri.exemple_carre_infinite: the class of [0,1]² is the sum of the classes of its sides, and is the sum of infinitely many families of translates (Remarque 1's hypotheses are satisfiable)

labels.label: bzdef:c3s2d1_somme_convexes

hypotheses.note: any real vector space, no dimension or topology

hypotheses.paper: p isomorphisme de ∏V_i sur W (pour les structures affines)
hypotheses.note: reading IsIsoConvexes (bijection, it and its inverse preserve two-point convex combinations); proved equivalent to plain bijectivity of p (isSommeConvexes_iff_bijOn), so every reading between 'bijection' and 'affine bijection with affine inverse' defines the same notion

questions: « isomorphisme … pour les structures affines » for convex sets that are not affine spaces: read as a bijection preserving convex combinations both ways (IsIsoConvexes). The notion of sum does not depend on this reading (isSommeConvexes_iff_bijOn), since p is linear.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r1_somme_classes

hypotheses.paper: K(E) the convex parts, E acting by translation
hypotheses.note: KE E = {s // Convex ℝ s} (∅ included), AddAction, KModE = orbit quotient

hypotheses.paper: first assertion (unique W' for every system V'_i)
hypotheses.note: remarque1_somme_unique, as printed, any finite I

hypotheses.paper: second assertion (every W' of class w is a sum of a family of classes v_i), no condition on n
« d'une infinité de façons si n ≠ 1 »
hypotheses.note: two distinct indices (n ≥ 2), Nontrivial E, W' nonempty

findings: benzecri1960_ch3.tex:312–319 (Remarque 1), degenerate cases only. (i) For n = 0 the second assertion is false: the empty family has sum {0}, so w = class of a point is the sum of the empty family of classes, but {1} (class w) is the sum of no family indexed by Fin 0 (Benzecri.not_remarque1_famille_fin_zero); hence also « une infinité de façons si n ≠ 1 » fails at n = 0. (ii) « une infinité de façons si n ≠ 1 » is false for empty convexes: in ℝ with n = 2, V_1 = V_2 = W = ∅, exactly one family of the classes has sum ∅ (Benzecri.not_remarque1_infinite_vide). (iii) It is also false for E = 0 (K(0) has two elements; argued, not formalized). Proved true form: n ≥ 1 for the second assertion (Benzecri.remarque1_famille); two distinct indices, E ≠ 0 and W' ≠ ∅ for the infinitude (Benzecri.remarque1_infinite). If Benzécri's convexes are nonempty, E ≠ 0 and n ≥ 1 is understood, the remark is correct as printed.
questions: Does K(E) contain the empty part, and is n ≥ 1 (resp. E ≠ 0) understood? Reading taken: ∅ ∈ K(E), n and E arbitrary; the degenerate failures are then reported as the finding above.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s2p1_decomposition_origine

hypotheses.paper: ∑ v_i = w, W of class w containing 0
hypotheses.note: any finite index set, n = 0 included; nothing added

findings: benzecri1960_ch3.tex:330–336: the proof asserts without argument that the translates V'_i − x'_i are the only systems through the origin with sum W (if U_i = V_i + a_i, 0 ∈ U_i, ∑U_i = W, why is U_i = V_i? A priori only ∑a_i stabilises W). The statement is true; the missing step is Benzecri.subset_of_translate_somme (compare the two decompositions of y/2 obtained from y + ∑a_i ∈ W and from −a_i ∈ V_i by a midpoint, then use injectivity of p). Not an error of the statement.

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r2_somme_infinie

hypotheses.paper: W and the V_i contain the origin

findings: benzecri1960_ch3.tex:350–353 (checked on the scan, p. 264: « (x ≠ o) » is printed): as worded, the definition only asks that each x ∈ W, x ≠ 0, be uniquely a finite sum of components; it omits that every finite sum of components lies in W. So worded it disagrees with Déf. 1 for a finite I: W = [0,1], V = [0,2] (one index) meets the wording but is not a sum in the sense of Déf. 1 (Benzecri.isSommeInfinieTexte_not_isSommeConvexes). Adding that condition is the only change needed (Benzecri.isSommeInfinie_iff_texte: the case x = 0 follows), and the result agrees with Déf. 1 for finite I (Benzecri.isSommeInfinie_iff_isSommeConvexes).
questions: Remarque 2's notion: reading taken = the sum map from finitely supported families (components in V_i) onto W is a bijection (IsSommeInfinie), i.e. the wording plus « every finite sum of components lies in W »; uniqueness of « une somme finie » read as uniqueness of the finitely supported family (components off N are 0, as the last sentence says). The literal wording is formalized too (IsSommeInfinieTexte).

labels.label: bzrem:c3s2r3_somme_directe

hypotheses.note: any subspace W (remarque3, remarque3_infinie: iSupIndep ∧ ⨆ = W); W = E gives DirectSum.IsInternal for Déf. 1 (finite I), for Remarque 2 in the reading and in the literal wording (any I)

questions: « au sens ci-dessus défini » read as both Déf. 1 (finite I) and Remarque 2 (any I); proved in each, and for Remarque 2 in both its reading and its literal wording, so no reading is needed.

kb_proposals: Sums of convex sets (Ch. 3 § 2): p = ∑ is linear, so « isomorphisme pour les structures affines » reduces to Set.BijOn (isSommeConvexes_iff_bijOn via isIsoConvexes_of_linear); work with BijOn and bijOn_vadd (translating each V_i by a_i translates W by ∑ a_i).
K(E)/E: KE E := {s // Convex ℝ s} with a hand-written AddAction; make KModE an `abbrev` of Quotient (AddAction.orbitRel …) or `rw [Quotient.eq]` fails on the def wrapper.

Finitely supported sums: define sommeF := Finsupp.lsum ℝ (fun _ => LinearMap.id) to get map_add/map_sub/map_smul for free; Submodule.mem_iSup_iff_exists_finsupp and iSupIndep_def + Finsupp.add_sum_erase' give iSupIndep ↔ injectivity on families (eq_zero_of_iSupIndep, iSupIndep_of_injOn).
Strict convexity of the Euclidean disc in ℝ×ℝ (sup norm there!): write it as {p | p.1^2+p.2^2 ≤ 1} and use the identity |αu+(1−α)v|² = α|u|²+(1−α)|v|² − α(1−α)|u−v|² (disque_strict).
